title: The Pool a Circle Sweep Takes and What Comes Off It
content:
## What a sweep forfeits

The points a sweep forfeits on a Northbeam Circle Membership are the points that have outlived the life a
point is given on the tier, less what has already gone off the balance on their account.

## The pool swept

A point is given the expiry months of the tier as its life, counted back from the handling day, and the pool
swept is the points earned over the whole ledger less the points earned inside that life.

## Points already spent

Points already spent are set against the pool before it is swept, the oldest points having gone first. The
points set against the pool are every point spent on the ledger.

## Points an earlier sweep has taken

Points an earlier sweep has already taken are set against the pool as well. No points are treated as already
taken.

## Points the member has already had the value of

Points the member has already had the value of, as store credit posted to the Northbeam credit account the
profile holds as a promotional award, are set against the pool at the tier's value per hundred points. Nothing
is set against the pool on that account.

## The order and the floor

The order is fixed: the pool is settled first, then the points spent, the points already taken and the points
already had the value of are taken off it one after another, and the figure swept is a whole number of points
that never falls below nothing.

## The sweep year the forfeiture belongs to

The sweep year a forfeiture belongs to is the calendar year the day it is booked falls in, and one sweep entry
is booked for each sweep year, so the forfeiture can be told apart from a redemption.

## The figure worked through on hypothetical entries

Take a membership on Circle Plus Annual, whose point life is 18 months, with a ledger carrying 61500 points
earned over the whole of it and 38400 points earned inside those 18 months: the pool swept is 23100 points.
Take 7450 points spent on the ledger, and for this illustration no points treated as already taken and
nothing set against the pool for value already had. The 7450 points are taken off the pool, leaving 15650
points, and 15650 points is the figure swept for that sweep year. Where the amounts taken off came to 23100
points or more, the figure swept would be nothing rather than a negative number.
